files.title: Multiannual Financial Framework 2028–2034
files.status: The Irish Presidency tabled a revised negotiating box on 10 October 2026 (Council doc 13922/26): €1,622bn in commitments at 2025 prices, 8% below the Commission proposal, with all figures in brackets. At the 15–16 October European Council, leaders asked António Costa to advance the talks; Agence Europe reported on 22 October that he will present his own negotiating box with figures ahead of a Special European Council on 26–27 November, still aiming for agreement in 2026. Unanimity in Council, then Parliament consent. Two programmes are followed as parts: the European Competitiveness Fund (ITRE co-rapporteurs Christian Ehler and Dan Nica; Council partial position on 16 June 2026) and the National and Regional Partnership Plans fund (BUDG, REGI and AGRI: Karlo Ressler, Andrey Novakov and Elsi Katainen), where Agence Europe reported a partial general approach on 16 June 2026.

files.title: Digital Omnibus on data: GDPR, ePrivacy, Data Act, NIS2
files.status: The Commission proposed it on 19 November 2025. Coreper II agreed the Council's negotiating mandate on 21 October 2026 (Council doc 14756/26): it keeps the current definition of personal data and adds a provision on pseudonymisation, keeps the ePrivacy cookie rules but drops consent for purposes such as audience measurement and device security, and replaces the single EU incident-reporting entry point with national entry points. In Parliament, the ITRE-LIBE draft report came out on 22 June 2026 and amendments were tabled on 27 July; no committee vote date is set, and talks with the Council start once Parliament has its position. Open fights: personal data and pseudonymisation, AI training on personal data, trade secrets under the Data Act, and the cookie rules.

files.title: Digital euro: establishment regulation
files.lede: Trilogues under way; data protection and exceptions for merchants are still open.
files.status: The Commission proposed it in June 2023. The Council agreed its position on 19 December 2025. Parliament's ECON adopted Fernando Navarrete's report on 23 June 2026 and plenary confirmed the mandate on 9 July. Trilogues are under way: the fifth, on 20 October, covered offline payment limits, anti-money-laundering rules for small payments and the long-term operating model. Still open: data protection, exceptions to merchant acceptance, cash acceptance, the roll-out and use outside the euro area. The ECB aims for issuance from 2029 if the law passes.

files.title: Food and feed safety omnibus (Omnibus X): pesticides, residues, GMOs, feed
files.lede: Council mandates done; Parliament's joint ENVI-AGRI committee still to vote.
files.status: The Commission proposed the omnibus on 16 December 2025: a regulation amending ten acts on pesticides, residue levels, GMOs, feed and official controls, and a directive amending related directives. In Parliament, a joint ENVI-AGRI committee leads with Michele Picaro (ECR, ENVI) and Herbert Dorfmann (EPP, AGRI); foodwatch criticised their draft report of 6 July for going further than the Commission on pesticide reviews.

files.title: European Research Area Act
files.lede: Commission proposal planned for 2026, not adopted yet.
files.status: The Commission plans to propose the ERA Act in 2026, brought forward from 2027 by Commissioner Ekaterina Zaharieva so it can pass in this mandate. It would add binding national commitments towards investing 3% of GDP in R&D, align EU and national research funding, and set conditions on research careers, research infrastructures and the freedom of scientific research. The consultation closed on 23 January 2026. Parliament adopted a resolution on the act on 10 March 2026, drafted by Eszter Lakos (EPP).

files.title: Military mobility regulation: moving troops and equipment across the EU
files.lede: Trilogues under way; the crisis mechanism is still to settle.

files.title: EU KIDS Act: minimum age for social media and safety by design for minors
files.lede: Proposed in September; a Council working party is on it; Parliament has not chosen its committee yet.
files.status: The Commission proposed the EU KIDS Act on 17 September 2026 (COM(2026)681). Social-networking and video-sharing platforms would have to check that account holders are 15 or older, with safety-by-design duties for services used by minors, a compliance plan for very large platforms, and Commission and AI Office supervision with fines up to 6% of turnover. The Observatory lists Stéphane Séjourné and DG GROW as responsible; Henna Virkkunen presented the proposal with the President. In the Council, the Audiovisual and Media Working Party has examined it since 2 October. In Parliament, the referral was announced on 22 October: IMCO leads, with opinions from SANT, ITRE, CULT, JURI and LIBE; no rapporteur is appointed yet.
